answer.concealment: A credit coordinator conceals from the trading desk that a margin or collateral call issued to a counterparty has already been formally waived by the coordinator, allowing the desk to continue treating the call as outstanding and the counterparty as in default, because admitting the waiver would expose that the coordinator unilaterally surrendered a remedy the desk was relying on as negotiating leverage.
answer.actor: Tana Jones — direct, efficient legal and credit coordinator who unilaterally waived the call
answer.victim: Sara Shackleton — task-oriented legal and regulatory coordinator who relies on the call as live leverage
answer.true_fact: The collateral call issued to Counterparty 7 (a Canadian energy trader appearing on the margin exception list) has already been formally waived by Tana Jones, who sent a written waiver letter to the counterparty's back office three days earlier without seeking approval from Sara Shackleton or the trading desk.
answer.false_belief: Sara Shackleton believes the collateral call against Counterparty 7 is still fully outstanding and enforceable, that the counterparty remains technically in default under the ISDA credit-support annex, and that the desk retains the right to demand immediate posting or declare an event of default — all of which Sara Shackleton intends to use as hard leverage in the upcoming margin-exception review meeting.
